patch.value: Release version replacement still rewrites a comment, not the exported extension identity

Tracks gh:unbraind/pm-jev#68 (filed 2026-10-29, missed by the blind issue watch). The release workflow's non-global first-match replacement (release.yml, source.replace(/version:\s*["'][^"']+["']/, ...)) still hits the explanatory comment above the export first: on current main index.ts line ~2471 holds the rewritten literal ('the release workflow rewrites the first version: "2026.10.31" literal') while the actual exported extension identity at line ~2475 still declares 2026.10.5, inconsistent with package.json/manifest.json at every release since. Fix the replacement to target the exported property (a global or anchored regex, or explicit capture of the export site) and add a release-prep regression asserting the exported identity equals the prepared version.

## Static release-identity mismatch
PR #67 head `321403235af39961d85a333be0c51120481dda84` prepares version `2026.10.29` in package.json, root lock metadata and manifest.json, but the actual default extension export still declares `2026.10.5` in both [index.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/321403235af39961d85a333be0c51120481dda84/index.ts#L2469-L2475) and [committed dist/index.js](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/321403235af39961d85a333be0c51120481dda84/dist/index.js#L1919-L1925).

The release diff updates the preceding comment's example `version: "2026.10.28"` to `.29`, not the actual exported property.

## Exact mechanism and bounded reproduction
[Release preparation, line153](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/321403235af39961d85a333be0c51120481dda84/.github/workflows/release.yml#L153) uses a non-global first-match replacement:
```js
source.replace(/version:\s*["'][^"']+["']/, 'version: "' + version + '"')
```
The first matching text is in the comment describing that replacement. A pure Node string-transform check using this public source excerpt, restoring only the comment's prior `.28` value and applying the exact regex with target `.29`, changes the comment while the export remains `2026.10.5`. Two assertions passed. No repository module, workflow, provider or native tracker was executed.

## Intended contract / impact
[Canonical release-readiness record pm-jev-release-gate](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/321403235af39961d85a333be0c51120481dda84/.agents/pm/chores/pm-jev-release-gate.toon), delivered by #51, requires verified metadata and packed release contents. The source itself describes the extension identity as release-managed.

Consumers inspecting the exported module receive a stale version inconsistent with the package/manifest, undermining reliable version attribution and diagnostics. Actual host display/cache behavior, installed package behavior and npm publication have **not** been tested or inferred. This is source/committed-output evidence, not a claim that this candidate is published.

All-status67issues/PRs and canonical issue/chore records checked. Existing #62 / #63 concern tarball argument resolution, not this identity mismatch. PR67 is the current candidate.

## Acceptance / regression
1. Update the actual exported identity structurally or from a single verified version source; do not match comments/string examples as code.
2. Fail release preparation when package, manifest and actual source/built default-export versions disagree.
3. Include a regression with a misleading version literal in a preceding comment and multiple unrelated version strings; check the exported property, not mere text presence.
4. Verify the packed artifact's actual extension export matches its package/manifest, without executing activation or contacting live providers.
5. Preserve approval/publishing guards and existing coverage thresholds; no release or credential change is requested by this issue.
Release version replacement updates a comment instead of the exported extension identity

value.text: Fix (branch fix/release-version-targets-extension-export), against the issue's acceptance list. (1) scripts/release-identity.ts --write replaces the release workflow's first-match regex. It sets only the version property of 'export default defineExtension({ name: "pm-jev", version: ... })' and refuses a source with zero or several such declarations, or a version that is not plain x.y.z. The index.ts comment no longer quotes a version literal, and the export now declares the package version 2026.11.4 (it had said 2026.10.5 since v0). (2) release:check runs verify:release-identity right after the build. It compares package.json, both package-lock.json versions, manifest.json and the version property of the source and built default exports, which are imported statically and never activated, so a mismatch fails release preparation before commit or publish. (3) test/release-identity.test.ts runs the rewrite on a fixture with a misleading preceding comment, catalog_version, a nested version and a --policy-version example, then evaluates the module in a child process: the old first-match rewrite leaves the export stale, the new one updates only the export. (4) The pack step runs --archive on ./release-artifact/package.tgz. The packed package.json and manifest.json must report the verified version, and the packed dist/index.js must be byte-identical to the build whose export was verified. The packed module is not evaluated, since an extracted archive has no dependencies. (5) No approval, publish or credential step changed; coverage stays at 100/100/100 including the new script. Revert check: restoring 2026.10.5 fails 'this repository's source and built exports report its package version'. Full release:check passed locally up to changelog:check, which needed this item's entry.
